claims.statement: deploy-harness.sh builds .claude/ as a derived copy of the root sources (skills, agents, hooks, rules, templates, runtime, settings.json), resolving sources by script path rather than git, and the same idempotent run serves first install and re-sync (update mode when .claude/settings.json already exists).

install-harness.sh fetches the harness source (shallow git clone or --source checkout), runs the source's deploy-harness.sh with --target and forwarded --yes/--overwrite-conflicts/--profile/--dry-run, then runs init-structure.sh; it never stages payload at the target root.

When the target already has .claude/settings.json, install-harness.sh requires consent to re-sync: --yes, --force, or --overwrite-conflicts, an interactive y answer, or else it fails without a controlling terminal; --force is an alias of --yes and does not overwrite protected files.

copy_dir merge-syncs per top-level entry: only entries the harness ships are removed and recopied, consumer-added entries are left untouched, agents/*.json adapter inputs are never copied, and local edits to non-protected harness files are overwritten on re-sync.

Deploy ships only an allow-listed subset of scripts/ (CONSUMER_SCRIPTS, which includes apply_model_config.py) into .claude/scripts/ plus harness-manifest.json, and rewrites root-relative helper paths to .claude/ paths in derived Markdown only, idempotently, leaving hooks byte-identical to source.

Deploy strips skills/_archive, skill tests (tests/ dirs and test_*.py), HARNESS_ONLY_DOCS, and harness-only fenced Markdown regions from the derived tree only, and its Markdown transforms never descend into .claude/worktrees or directories with their own .git entry.

Orphan pruning removes only entries listed in the previous .claude/.harness-deployed manifest that were not deployed this run, so consumer additions are never pruned and a first deploy prunes nothing.

Hook profiles come from harness-manifest.json hook_profiles: minimal registers branch-isolation-guard.sh and commit-gate.sh, standard (the default) and strict register those plus session-knowledge.sh and model-config.sh, and the profile is passed to commit-gate.sh as --profile

which selects its check set (minimal runs only the secrets scan; strict adds untracked-.py and app gates).

Deploy resolves the profile from an explicit --profile, else a valid value in .claude/.harness-profile, else the manifest default; an unknown profile aborts before any write, and the resolved profile is written back to .claude/.harness-profile so flagless re-syncs reuse it.

derive_settings filters root settings.json hooks to the profile's hook list, drops emptied groups and events, prefixes relative commands with $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/, and appends --profile

only to the commit-gate command.

derive_settings merges into an existing .claude/settings.json: foreign top-level keys and foreign hooks are preserved, any current harness command or command under $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/ is stripped and the derived harness hooks re-added (no double registration, removed harness hooks pruned), and events left empty are removed.
An existing .claude/settings.json that is not valid JSON is backed up to settings.json.invalid-bak-<timestamp> with a warning before a fresh harness settings.json is written.

BOOTSTRAP_OWNED_FILES (rules/architecture.md, rules/guidelines.md, rules/behavior.md, agents/PROJECT.md) are protected: a single preflight before any write detects local-vs-incoming differences and resolves one batch policy — overwrite with --overwrite-conflicts, keep with --yes or no controlling terminal, otherwise an interactive keep/overwrite/backup/abort prompt read from /dev/tty.

Under the keep policy the local protected file is retained and the incoming version is saved as <file>.harness-incoming; backup copies the local file into .claude/.harness-backup-<ts>/ before overwriting; an identical protected file triggers removal of any stale sidecar.

For a protected file nested inside a synced directory (agents/PROJECT.md), sync_protected_dir snapshots the local file and any .proposed draft, copies the directory wholesale, then reconciles per policy and always restores the local .proposed — sound only because the harness ships no .proposed files.
deploy --dry-run reports protected-file conflicts and would-be prunes then exits 0 before anything under .claude/ is written, and the installer's --dry-run writes nothing to the target.
init-structure.sh copies templates/structure files to specs/, docs/solutions/, and techstacks/ destinations only when the destination does not exist, printing created/exists and always exiting 0.

After a non-dry-run install, install-harness.sh appends .claude/ to the target .gitignore unless .claude is already tracked by git or an existing directory-scoped .claude rule exists; appends never rewrite existing lines and a failure only warns.

The installer also appends specs/**/events.jsonl.lock to .gitignore unless git check-ignore shows the deciding rule for a probe lock path already comes from a .gitignore file (including a negation the consumer chose).

Before any write under .claude/ (and also under --dry-run), check_model_config renders the model/effort defaults snapshot from source and validates the target's root harness-models.json with apply_model_config.py --check; on failure deploy exits 1 with nothing written, so a first deploy creates no .claude/ and a re-sync changes no file.

After rewrite_derived_paths, apply_model_config copies the defaults snapshot to .claude/harness-models.defaults.json and runs apply_model_config.py --apply, which rewrites only model/effort frontmatter lines of snapshot-named agents/<role>.md and skills/<name>/SKILL.md, never settings files, leaving consumer skills untouched and making repeat deploys idempotent.
If scripts/apply_model_config.py is missing from the harness source, deploy warns and skips both the model-config check and the apply step rather than failing.
